subject: Post-demo compliance recap: EU region, SOC 2 timeline & ITAR/OFAC screening
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@medsys.eu>, Anna Müller <anna.mueller@northhealth.de>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-30T14:12:00+01:00
Subject: Post-demo compliance recap: EU region, SOC 2 timeline & ITAR/OFAC screening

Hi Simon / Anna,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary from demo: 
- Redwood can serve models from an EU region (Frankfurt / Amsterdam) and supports tenant-level data residency controls.
- We showed a hosted flow and a Dedicated/Private option for stricter isolation.
- We discussed SOC 2 posture (we have Type II in progress; bridge letter attached) and the vendor questionnaire you shared.

Open items / asks for you: 
1) Can you confirm whether any of the datasets you plan to send fall under ITAR or other export restrictions? If yes, which dataset(s) and the controlling classification.
2) Do you have a hard requirement for data to remain within the EU (no cross-border egress) or is a contractual assurance sufficient?
3) Please flag any specific OFAC/embargoed-entity concerns so our export controls team can run screening.

Our immediate next steps (what we will do):
- Attach: SOC2-bridge-letter.pdf and the Redwood vendor questionnaire (xlsx).
- Start the vendor security questionnaire intake; Laura will own coordination on our side.
- If you need ITAR-only processing, we can outline an on-prem/private deployment path and provide a high-level quote.

Proposed short timeline:
- 1–2 business days: confirm dataset classification & residency constraint (from you)
- 3–5 business days: completed vendor questionnaire and initial export screening call with our compliance team
- 2–4 weeks: more detailed SOC 2 artifacts/controls mapping depending on the items requested

Would you be available for a 30-minute compliance call next week (suggested: Tue 2027-04-05 09:00–11:00 CET)? If so, I’ll send a calendar invite and include our compliance lead.

Attachments: SOC2-bridge-letter.pdf; redwood-vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
From: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@medsys.eu>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@northhealth.de>
Date: 2027-03-30T16:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo compliance recap: EU region, SOC 2 timeline & ITAR/OFAC screening

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the clear recap — helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 
- We are EU-first; data residency inside the EU is a strong preference, but we might accept contractual controls for specific non-sensitive telemetry.
- We are unsure about ITAR status on two datasets currently — I will check with our regulatory team and confirm by tomorrow.
- On OFAC: we do business in some non-embargoed jurisdictions; no known sanctions at the moment, but we will run an internal screening and share any flagged entities.

One question: does Redwood run an entity screening automatically as part of onboarding, or do we need to provide lists for you to check? Also, for the private deployment path, can you share a short note on the typical lead time and whether we can host in our Azure Frankfurt tenancy?

I can take Tue 2027-04-05 10:00 CET for a compliance call. Please include the compliance lead if you have them available.

Best,
Simon
Director of IT & Compliance
MediSys GmbH

Date: 2027-03-31T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: coordinate intake + questionnaire (internal)

Karthik / Dev,

Thanks — I’ll own the vendor questionnaire intake for MediSys. Suggested plan: 
- I’ll send the redwood-vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx to Simon and Anna with our pre-filled answers for the common sections (network controls, encryption at rest / in transit, IAM).
- Dev, can you prepare a 1-page technical note that covers: 
  - Which regions support zero-egress (tenant-level residency) and any limitations (model variants, cold storage).
  - The Private deployment offer: estimated lead time (4–6 weeks to provision in customer-managed VNet) and required network/VPN details for Azure FR.
  - Our standard export control screening steps (entity screening, OFAC checks, ITAR escalation path).

Compliance flow for ITAR/OFAC-sensitive datasets: 
1) Initial intake + dataset classification (customer)
2) Screening (we run automated OFAC/entity check)
3) If ITAR flagged -> escalate to Export Compliance team for eligibility; recommend Private/on-prem deployment for restricted workloads

Timeline: We can have the questionnaire back to them within 3 business days once we have the missing dataset classification answers from Simon.

I’ll also prep a short list of artifacts we can share (bridge letter, selected SOC 2 controls mapping, encryption & key management notes). Karthik — loop me into the call on Apr 5.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance (Sales Support)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Leclerc <simon.leclerc@medsys.eu>
Cc: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@northhealth.de>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo compliance recap: EU region, SOC 2 timeline & ITAR/OFAC screening

Hi Simon — quick follow-up and answers to your questions: 

1) Entity screening: we run an automated OFAC and global watchlist screening on all external counterparties during vendor intake. If you have a pre-populated list of vendors/entities you plan to reference, feel free to share it; otherwise we will run our default checks.

2) Private deployment in Azure FR: yes — we can deploy into a customer-managed Azure subscription in Frankfurt. Dev has started a 1-page note (attached link) that outlines required network config (VPN/ExpressRoute, NSG recommendations). Typical lead time: 4–6 weeks from signed PO and network readiness.

3) ITAR/OFAC-sensitive datasets: If your regulatory team confirms ITAR-controlled data, we recommend Private deployment (on-prem or customer VNet) and an export-eligibility review. We will triage eligibility quickly but note that ITAR approvals can extend the timeline depending on the classification.

Next actions: 
- Simon: confirm dataset classification by EOD 2027-04-03 (yes/no for ITAR; any flagged OFAC entities).
- Laura: send the pre-filled questionnaire and SOC 2 artifacts link to Simon (please include the bridge letter and controls summary).
- Dev: attach the technical note link in the calendar invite for Apr 5.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue Apr 5 10:00 CET and include our compliance lead. If anything changes, reply-all.

Best,
Karthik
